result.what_interviewer_wanted: Explain why using a mutable default argument like an empty list is dangerous in Python, including the evaluation of default values at function definition and the recommendation to use None.
result.improved_answer: I haven’t yet had to deal with mutable defaults in a project, but I know that in Python default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined. If you use a mutable object like a list, that same list is shared across all calls, so data from one call can leak into another. The usual fix is to set the default to None and create a new list inside the function.
